name: TLV62569DBVR
title: TLV62569, TLV62569P: 2-A synchronous step-down converter, 2.5 V to 5.5 V input, in SOT packages
summary: A synchronous buck converter with both FETs on chip (100 mΩ high side, 60 mΩ low side) that delivers up to 2 A from a 2.5 V to 5.5 V input. The output is set from 0.6 V up to VIN by an external divider. It runs PWM near 1.5 MHz under load and drops into power save mode at light load, draws 35 µA quiescent and under 2 µA shut down, and can run at 100 % duty cycle. Soft start, current limit, UVLO and thermal shutdown are built in; the TLV62569P adds an open-drain power-good output. Packages are SOT23-5 (DBV), SOT23-6 (DDC) and SOT563-6 (DRL).

notes: All are active, production parts.
The P in TLV62569P marks the version with a power-good output (DDC and DRL packages). The DBV and plain DRL versions have none; on the DRL the sixth pin is NC.
Marking symbols: TLV62569DBV 16AF, TLV62569DRL 19D, TLV62569PDRL 19E; TLV62569PDDC 7G, and (6D9, 6DW) for the orderable TLV62569PDDCR and TLV62569PDDCT parts.
Body size, nominal: SOT23 (5) and SOT23 (6) 2.90 mm × 2.80 mm; SOT563 (6) 1.60 mm x 1.60 mm.
Two markings in parentheses are alternatives; a part carries one of them.

circuits.title: 1.8-V output application
circuits.description: A 1.8 V, 2 A step-down supply running from 2.5 V to 5.5 V on the power-good version. EN is tied to VIN. L1 and C2 filter the switch node into the output; C1 is the input reservoir at VIN. R1 and R2 divide the output down to the 0.6 V feedback reference, giving 0.6 V × (1 + 200k/100k) = 1.8 V. R3 pulls the open-drain PG output up to the input rail and brings it out as VPG. C3 across R1 is an optional feed-forward capacitor that speeds the load-transient response; 6.8 pF suits R2 = 100 kΩ.
notes: C3 is optional; the rest of the circuit is the same with or without it.

operation.text: Peak-current control with an adaptive off time. The off time of the low-side FET is set from the VIN/VOUT ratio, which keeps the switching frequency near 1.5 MHz in PWM across changes in input, output and load. PWM is used at moderate and heavy load.

When the inductor current goes discontinuous at light load, the converter moves to power save mode on its own: it switches less often and draws less supply current. The output then sits a little above its nominal value; a larger output capacitor shrinks that offset.

As the input falls toward the output, the device goes to 100 % duty cycle: the high-side FET stays on and the low-side FET stays off, so the dropout is the load current times the high-side on-resistance plus the inductor DCR (Equation 1).

After enable, an internal soft start ramps the output to its set point over tSS (800 µs typ for the DBV version, 900 µs typ for the others). This limits inrush current, gives a smooth rise and keeps high-impedance sources such as batteries from sagging. The converter starts correctly into an output capacitor that is already charged, ramping from that voltage.

The high-side switch current is sensed. When it reaches ILIM (3 A min for DBV and DDC, 2.5 A min for DRL), the high-side FET turns off and the low-side FET turns on, letting the inductor current fall for an adaptive off time. This guards against heavy loads and output shorts.
Below VUVLO (2.3 V typ, VIN falling) the device shuts down; it restarts once VIN rises past the threshold plus about 100 mV of hysteresis.
The device stops at a junction temperature of about 150 °C and resumes on its own once it has cooled to about 130 °C.
A logic high on EN starts switching and regulation; a logic low shuts the device down, where it draws 0.1 µA typ. EN has to be tied to a defined level.

On the TLV62569P, PG is an open-drain output rated to sink 1 mA. It releases (high impedance) once the output passes 95 % of nominal and pulls low when the output drops below about 90 %, after a 40 µs delay. It needs a pull-up to a rail under 5.5 V and may drive the EN pin of a following converter to sequence rails. PG is also low in shutdown, thermal shutdown and UVLO; with VIN below 1.4 V it is high impedance. Unused, it is left open.

Ceramic capacitors with low ESR, X7R or X5R, are suited to both input and output. 4.7 µF at the input is enough in most designs; more reduces input ripple. The output capacitor may range from 10 µF to 47 µF, paired with the inductor as in the output capacitor and inductor combinations.

A capacitor across the upper divider resistor raises the loop bandwidth for a faster transient response; 6.8 pF is the value for R2 = 100 kΩ. TI application report SLVA289 covers the trade between stability and transient response.

Choose the inductance first, then a saturation current about 20 % to 30 % above the peak current from Equation 3, also weighing DC resistance and size. The tested output filter pairs use 1 µH or 2.2 µH; 2.2 µH is the standard choice.
The source feeding VIN needs a current rating that fits the input voltage, the output voltage and the load current.

Put the input capacitor, output capacitor and inductor as near the IC as possible and run the power traces short, direct and wide to keep resistance and stray inductance low. Return the ground terminals of both the input capacitor and the output capacitor solidly to power ground so the ground reference does not shift. Treat the FB connection as a sensitive signal and route it away from the SW node; ground layers may serve as shielding. In the DBV example C1 sits beside the IC from VIN to GND, L1 runs from the SW pin to the VOUT copper, C2 sits from VOUT to GND on the other side of the IC, and R1 and R2 sit below by the FB pin. In the PDRL example C1 and C2 sit either side of the IC, L1 below it, and R1 and R2 above it.

Power dissipation in these small packages depends on the board and the system around it: airflow, coupling to nearby parts, the surfaces available for convection, and other hot components. Heat removal improves through the PCB design and through added airflow. TI reports SZZA017 and SPRA953 explain the thermal metrics.
